newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-PIAZZA TOPS VOTING AS NL ALL-STAR STARTERS NAMED.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-PIAZZA TOPS VOTING AS NL ALL-STAR STARTERS NAMED.

text.p: Mike Piazza of the Los Angeles Dodgers will be the National League starting catcher for the fourth consecutive year after receiving the most votes in final fan balloting announced Tuesday for next week's All-Star Game.

Piazza will be the lone starter from the Dodgers, while the Houston Astros and San Diego Padres each placed two players in the starting lineup for the 68th All-Star Game next Tuesday at Jacobs Field in Cleveland.

Piazza, who is batting .365 with 16 home runs, topped the National League voting for the second successive year with 2,626,213 votes. Seattle Mariners outfielder Ken Griffey Jr. was the leading vote-getter in the majors, receiving 3,514,340 votes in American League balloting announced Monday.
The Astros will be represented by first baseman Jeff Bagwell and second baseman Craig Biggio, who was chosen for the sixth straight season.
Third baseman Ken Caminiti, the 1996 NL Most Valuable Player, and future Hall of Famer Tony Gwynn, who is hitting .392, will represent the Padres in the starting lineup.

Gwynn, who collected 1,603,730 votes to edge out Barry Bonds of the San Francisco Giants (1,559,313) for the third and final outfield position, was chosen to the All-Star team for the 13th time in his brilliant career.
The other NL outfield starters will be Kenny Lofton of the Atlanta Braves and Colorado's Larry Walker, who is hitting .408 with 25 home runs.
Lofton will appear as a National League All-Star for the first time after competing each of the last three years for the American League as a member of the Cleveland Indians.
Barry Larkin of the Cincinnati Reds was voted to start at shortstop, but is currently on the disabled list. Larkin, named to his ninth All-Star team, said he did not think he would play if selected.
The pitchers and reserves for both teams will be chosen by managers Joe Torre of the Yankees and Bobby Cox of the Braves and announced Wednesday.
